from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.array(im)
print("shape:", a.shape)

# Detect stripe boundaries: columns where color changes significantly
# Compute column-averaged colors
cols = a.mean(axis=0)  # (W, 3)

# find boundaries by diff between adjacent columns
diffs = np.abs(np.diff(cols.astype(int), axis=0)).sum(axis=1)
threshold = 20
bounds = np.where(diffs > threshold)[0]
# collapse consecutive
bounds_c = []
for b in bounds:
    if not bounds_c or b - bounds_c[-1] > 1:
        bounds_c.append(b)
print("num boundaries:", len(bounds_c))
print("first 40 boundaries:", bounds_c[:40])
print("gaps between consecutive boundaries:", np.diff(bounds_c)[:40])
EOF

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.array(im)
cols = a.mean(axis=0)

# Merge with tolerance and describe each run
runs = []
start = 0
for x in range(1, 1000):
    if np.abs(cols[x]-cols[x-1]).sum() > 12:
        runs.append((start, x)); start = x
runs.append((start, 1000))

# Merge runs narrower than 3 px into neighbors (edge artifacts)
# Compute average color per run
def avg_color(s,e):
    return cols[s:e].mean(axis=0)

out = []
for s,e in runs:
    c = avg_color(s,e)
    r,g,b = [int(round(v)) for v in c]
    lum = 0.2126*r+0.7152*g+0.0722*b
    out.append((s,e,e-s,(r,g,b),lum))

print(f"{'start':>5} {'end':>5} {'w':>4}  {'RGB':>15} {'lum':>6}")
for s,e,w,c,l in out:
    print(f"{s:>5} {e:>5} {w:>4}  {str(c):>15} {l:>6.1f}")
EOF

from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')

for i in range(10):
    seg = slice(i*100,(i+1)*100)
    print(f"  x={i*100:4d}-{(i+1)*100:4d}: R-B = {warm[seg].mean():+.1f}   meanRGB=({r[seg].mean():.0f},{g[seg].mean():.0f},{b[seg].mean():.0f})")

# Blue-ness (B-R) in 20 segments
print("\nBlueness (B-R) in 20 segments of 50px:")
for i in range(20):
    seg = slice(i*50,(i+1)*50)
    print(f"  x={i*50:4d}-{(i+1)*50:4d}: B-R = {(b[seg]-r[seg]).mean():+.1f}")
EOF

"**Shape of You**" is a song by English singer [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"). It was released on 6 January 2017 as one of the [double lead singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from his third studio album *[÷](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/÷_\(album\) "÷ (album)")* (2017), along with "[Castle on the Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_on_the_Hill "Castle on the Hill")". The [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall_pop "Dancehall pop") and [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues") infused song was written by Sheeran, [Steve Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Mac "Steve Mac") and [Johnny McDaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_McDaid "Johnny McDaid"). Due to its [interpolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpolation_\(popular_music\) "Interpolation (popular music)") of "[No Scrubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Scrubs "No Scrubs")" by [TLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TLC_\(group\) "TLC (group)"), [Kandi Burruss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandi_Burruss "Kandi Burruss"), [Tameka "Tiny" Cottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tameka_Cottle "Tameka Cottle"), and [Kevin "She'kspere" Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_"She'kspere"_Briggs "Kevin \"She'kspere\" Briggs") are also credited as writers. The song was produced by Sheeran and Steve Mac.

Despite receiving mixed reviews from music critics, "Shape of You" peaked at number one on the singles charts of 34 countries, including the [US *Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100")—later becoming the [best performing song of 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2017 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2017")—as well as in the British, Australian, Canadian and Irish[\[2\]](#cite_note-IRE-2) singles charts. It stayed at number one for a record-tying 16 consecutive weeks on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), as well as 14 nonconsecutive weeks on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"), and 12 non-consecutive weeks on the Billboard Hot 100\. It was also highly successful elsewhere, reaching number one in many European charts and throughout [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America"),[\[3\]](#cite_note-ARG-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-COL-4) as well as in [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia") where it spent 12 non-consecutive weeks at the top.[\[5\]](#cite_note-MAL-5)

On 10 December 2018, the song became the first song to hit 2 billion streams on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"). On July 13, 2026, “Shape of You” became the second song to reach 5 billion streams on the platform and is currently the 2nd most streamed song overall, behind "[Blinding Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinding_Lights "Blinding Lights")" by [The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd").[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) It was also the most-streamed song of the decade on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") with 2\.4 billion streams by December 2019, and the most streamed song on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") with 930 million streams, as of May 2023\. It was the best-selling song of 2017 and the decade in the UK. "Shape of You" was the best-selling song of 2017 and the second best-selling digital song worldwide, with combined sales and track-equivalent streams of 26\.6 million units according to [IFPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry").[\[7\]](#cite_note-ifpi_report-7)

In 2018, it sold an additional 14\.9 million copies, combining a total of 41\.5 million copies worldwide with the previous total sales figure, making it one of the [best selling digital singles of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles#Best-selling_digital_singles "List of best-selling singles"). Additionally, it made a second appearance in the *Billboard* year-end chart in 2018, at No. 71\.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) In 2019, it was named the number-one song on the *Billboard* [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") chart of the 2010s decade.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) "Shape of You" was nominated for [British Single of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Single "Brit Award for British Single") and [British Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Video_of_the_Year "Brit Award for British Video of the Year") at the [2018 Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Brit_Awards "2018 Brit Awards").[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) The song won the [Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance") at the [60th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "60th Annual Grammy Awards").[\[11\]](#cite_note-Grammys-11) In 2021, *Billboard* ranked "Shape of You" as the tenth most successful song of all time.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

Written and recorded in 2016,[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) "Shape of You" was the final song added to Ed Sheeran's third album *[÷](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/÷_\(album\) "÷ (album)")*.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) As he had recently written all the songs he wanted for the album, the song was therefore not intended to be included in the album. It was first written for [Little Mix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Mix "Little Mix") and then it was conceived as a duet between [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") and [Rudimental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudimental "Rudimental"), but the head of the record label convinced him to keep the song for himself.[\[15\]](#cite_note-braca-15) He said:

> "\['Shape of You'\] is actually a really random one because I went in to write songs for other people with a guy called [Steve Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Mac "Steve Mac") and [Johnny McDaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_McDaid "Johnny McDaid"), and we were writing this song and I was like 'this would really work for Rihanna,'" he explained. "And then I started singing lyrics like 'putting [Van the Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison "Van Morrison") on the jukebox' and I was like 'well she's not really going to sing that, is she?' And then we sort of decided halfway through that we were just going to make it for me."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

According to Sheeran, Steve Mac started the songwriting session by playing the opening notes of the song on the keyboard. Sheeran then joined in, adding percussion by tapping on the guitar, layering it onto the track. On the writing of the song, he said that he tried to keep the music "more stripped" instead of something more elaborate: "I'm an [acoustic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_music "Acoustic music") artist, first and foremost. And when I play live, I can't replicate these things, I haven't got all the other musicians." Sheeran said he wanted an [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") feel to the song, therefore he adjusted the original tune, adding an interpolation of "[No Scrubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Scrubs "No Scrubs")" onto part of the melody. He also revealed that the original lyrics did not end with the words "the shape of you" in the chorus, but during the writing of the song, McDaid thought that the lyrics "I'm in love with your body" sounded objectifying, and the lyrics was therefore adjusted.[\[17\]](#cite_note-nytimes-17)[\[15\]](#cite_note-braca-15) In a March 2023 interview with *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*, Sheeran revealed that he had attempted to get a [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z") guest verse; Jay-Z declined, stating that he "doesn't think the song needs a [rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapping "Rapping") verse".[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

## Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release")\]

On 6 January 2017, when hosting *[The Radio 1 Breakfast Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Radio_1_Breakfast_Show "The Radio 1 Breakfast Show")*, Sheeran revealed that "Shape of You" was written with Rihanna in mind.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) On 4 January 2017, Sheeran uploaded a six-second teaser video of a blue background to social media, with lyrics "the club isn't the best place to find a lover", which is the first line of "Shape of You". To further tease the release, Sheeran and his label used a sponsored [Snapchat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapchat "Snapchat") lens filter with 30 seconds of the song to increase buzz among the general public.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Composition")\]

"Shape of You" has been characterised as [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"),[\[22\]](#cite_note-McIntyre-22) [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall"),[\[23\]](#cite_note-:0-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) and [tropical house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_house "Tropical house"),[\[25\]](#cite_note-Molanphy_2022-25) with "strummy acoustics".[\[26\]](#cite_note-auto-26) "Shape of You" is written in the key of [C-sharp minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-sharp_minor "C-sharp minor") with a tempo of 96 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute"). The song is composed in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature") (**4**  
**4** time), and follows a basic [chord progression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chord_progression "Chord progression") of C♯m–F♯m–A–B (i–iv–VI–VII), and Sheeran's vocals span from G♯3 to G♯5.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) It has a [tresillo rhythm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tresillo_\(rhythm\) "Tresillo (rhythm)").[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)

In the song, Sheeran sings over a [marimba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marimba "Marimba")\-fueled percussive sway about a budding romance: "The club isn't the best place to find a lover, so the bar is where I go/ Me and my friends at the table doing shots drinking fast and then we talk slow", he sings. "Come over and start up a conversation with just me/ And trust me I'll give it a chance."[\[29\]](#cite_note-29)[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) According to *[NT News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NT_News "NT News")*, the song "tells the story of loved (or lusted) up Sheeran meeting a girl in a bar where he and his mates are doing shots."[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

The song's lyrical rhythm drew some comparisons to the 1999 [TLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TLC_\(group\) "TLC (group)") hit "[No Scrubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Scrubs "No Scrubs")", particularly in the pre-chorus line, "Boy, let's not talk too much/ Grab on my waist and put that body on me". Kandi Burruss had told Bravo's Andy Cohen that the negotiations had started before the song's release for its interpolation but weren't finalized until afterwards. As a result, the composers of "No Scrubs", [Kandi Burruss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandi_Burruss "Kandi Burruss"), [Tameka "Tiny" Cottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tameka_Cottle "Tameka Cottle"), and [Kevin "She'kspere" Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_"She'kspere"_Briggs "Kevin \"She'kspere\" Briggs"), received co-writing credits on "Shape of You".[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

The song received generally mixed reviews from music critics. [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") from *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* said, "'Shape of You' is trickier, a nimble and effective song that takes the aggressive thinning of '[Caribbean music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_music "Caribbean music")'."[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")*'s Taylor Weatherby wrote about the song saying, "'Shape of You' doesn't quite sound like your typical Sheeran tune. But that almost serves as an indication of what the '[Thinking Out Loud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thinking_Out_Loud "Thinking Out Loud")' singer has been up to during his hiatus: creating music that still feels like Sheeran, just with a new twist."[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) Jeremy Gordon of *[Spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_\(magazine\) "Spin (magazine)")* gave the song a positive review, stating that the song "is a plausible attempt at convincing us he has had sex ... a lot of it. It kind of slaps, though you can't really picture Sheeran ever saying 'put that body on me' to a real human woman."[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) *[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")* gave the song a B+ rating,[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) and *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* ranked the song at number 13 on its "50 best songs of 2017" list.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) *[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")* ranked it at number 36 of 2017 singles.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)

*[Uproxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uproxx "Uproxx")* ranked the song at number 3 on its "The Worst Songs Of 2017" list: "The contrarian in me is always tempted to defend Ed Sheeran, because it's way too easy to take shots at this guy... Then I hear the part in 'Shape Of You' where he says, 'And last night you were in my room / And now my bedsheets smell like you.' And now I want to push him into a locker."[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) *Spin* and *[Esquire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esquire_\(magazine\) "Esquire (magazine)")* listed it as one of the worst songs of 2017\.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)[\[41\]](#cite_note-41)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"Shape of You" debuted at number one on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") on 13 January 2017, selling 227,000 combined units in its first week and becoming Sheeran's third UK number one. Sheeran also debuted at number two with the song "[Castle on the Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_on_the_Hill "Castle on the Hill")", making him the first artist in UK chart history to debut in the top two positions simultaneously.[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) It spent 13 consecutive weeks at number one,[\[43\]](#cite_note-weeks-43) and a further week at the top after a week's interruption by [Harry Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Styles "Harry Styles")' "[Sign of the Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sign_of_the_Times_\(Harry_Styles_song\) "Sign of the Times (Harry Styles song)")".[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) In July 2017, the song reached 184 million in streams, making it the most-streamed song in the UK of all time until November 2022, when it was overtaken by [Lewis Capaldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Capaldi "Lewis Capaldi")'s "[Someone You Loved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Someone_You_Loved "Someone You Loved")".[\[45\]](#cite_note-45) It was the nation's highest selling and most streamed track of 2017 with 787,000 copies sold and 248 million streams throughout the year, to produce a combined sales of 3\.2 million.[\[46\]](#cite_note-Top40UK2017-46) In September 2020, the track was [certified eight-times platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_music_recording_certifications "List of music recording certifications") by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI).[\[47\]](#cite_note-BPI-47) "Shape of You" is Sheeran's best-selling single in the UK with total sales of 5\.09 million units as of July 2021, according to the [Official Charts Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company").[\[48\]](#cite_note-OCC-48)

The song debuted at number one on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), selling 240,000 downloads and gaining 20 million streams in its debut week in the US, becoming Sheeran's first number one song in the country.[\[49\]](#cite_note-Billboard_record-49) Sheeran also became the first artist to debut two songs in the top 10 the same week in the history of the Hot 100, with "Castle on the Hill" also debuting at number six.[\[49\]](#cite_note-Billboard_record-49) "Shape of You" topped the Hot 100 for 12 non-consecutive weeks.[\[50\]](#cite_note-trust-50) In its fourth week at number one, the song also topped the [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40"), becoming Sheeran's second number-one single on the chart (after 2015's "Thinking Out Loud"). On 6 May 2017, it fell to number two on the Hot 100, being displaced by [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar")'s "[Humble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humble_\(song\) "Humble (song)")".[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) On the issue date, 2 September 2017, "Shape of You" spent its 32nd week in the top ten of Hot 100, tying the record for the most weeks on that chart with [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes")' "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")" and [the Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chainsmokers "The Chainsmokers")' "[Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Closer (The Chainsmokers song)")" featuring [Halsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halsey_\(singer\) "Halsey (singer)").[\[52\]](#cite_note-us_sales1-52) The following week, "Shape of You" spent its 33rd consecutive week in the top 10, breaking the 20-year-old record. This record would be tied twice and eventually broken in 2020 by [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone")'s "[Circles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circles_\(Post_Malone_song\) "Circles (Post Malone song)")."[\[53\]](#cite_note-53) On [*Billboard*'s Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay") chart, "Shape of You" became Sheeran's first number one on a Dance/EDM chart (his third top ten and sixth overall at Dance/Mix Show Airplay) in the United States.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) Afterwards, the song topped [Dance Club Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") in its 18 March 2017 issue, his first as a solo artist and his second entry on this chart, when he was a featured artist on Rudimental's "[Lay It All on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lay_It_All_on_Me_\(song\) "Lay It All on Me (song)")", which peaked at No. 38 in 2016\.[\[55\]](#cite_note-US_Dance_current_number_one-55)[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) By August 2017, "Shape of You" was the best selling song of 2017 in the US with 2\.3 million copies sold, the only one to sell over two million. It is also the most streamed song with 799\.7 million combined audio and video streams.[\[52\]](#cite_note-us_sales1-52) The song became the number one song of the year on *Billboard* Hot 100 in 2017,[\[57\]](#cite_note-57) and the second best-selling song in the US after "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")" with over 2\.5 million copies sold.[\[58\]](#cite_note-us_sales-58)

It debuted at number one in France,[\[59\]](#cite_note-France-59) and was later certified diamond there.[\[60\]](#cite_note-60) According to [Pure Charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pure_Charts "Pure Charts"), in the first half of the year 2017, the song reached 631,000 units (105,000 sales and 526,000 units from streams) and as of September 2017, it exceeds 812,109 units (707,109 from streams).[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) It was the best-selling song (including streaming) in France this year.[\[62\]](#cite_note-62) In [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts"), the song stayed at No. 1 for 15 weeks, breaking a record set 22 years ago by [Coolio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coolio "Coolio")'s "[Gangsta's Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangsta's_Paradise "Gangsta's Paradise")".[\[63\]](#cite_note-63) In doing this, it also broke ABBA's record of fourteen weeks at number one, which was set on the previous Australian charts before the ARIA charts became Australia's official charts.[\[64\]](#cite_note-64) "Shape of You" was also Australia's highest selling song of 2017 with 630,000 copies sold by the end of the year.[\[65\]](#cite_note-AustraliaEnd2017-65) The song is the first ever number one single of the now-defunct [Philippine Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Hot_100 "Philippine Hot 100") upon the chart's inception on 12 June 2017\.[\[66\]](#cite_note-66) It stayed at the peak position for 4 consecutive weeks before it was dethroned by "Despacito" by [Luis Fonsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Fonsi "Luis Fonsi") and [Daddy Yankee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy_Yankee "Daddy Yankee") featuring [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber").\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

Worldwide, the song reached one billion streams on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") in June 2017\.[\[67\]](#cite_note-67)[\[68\]](#cite_note-68) It became the most streamed song on Spotify in September 2017, reaching 1,318,420,396 streams overtaking [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)")'s "[One Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Dance "One Dance")".[\[69\]](#cite_note-spotify-69) It became the first song to reach [2 billions in streams on Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records "List of Spotify streaming records") in 2018,[\[70\]](#cite_note-forbes-70) and it was the most-streamed song of the decade on Spotify, with 2\.4 billion streams in the 2010s.[\[71\]](#cite_note-decade_stream-71) On 22 December 2021, "Shape of You" became Spotify's first song to hit 3 billion streams.[\[72\]](#cite_note-72) In May 2023, [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") announced that "Shape of You" was the most-streamed song on the platform, with over 930 million streams.[\[73\]](#cite_note-73)[\[74\]](#cite_note-74)

In August 2018, *Billboard* published a new edition of the "Greatest of All Time Hot 100 Singles" chart, its list of the 100 best-performing songs in the history of the Hot 100\. "Shape of You" was ranked at number nine, the third-highest position of any song released in the 2010s (behind only "[Uptown Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")" by [Mark Ronson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ronson "Mark Ronson") featuring [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars") and "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")" by [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO "LMFAO") featuring [Lauren Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauren_Bennett "Lauren Bennett") and [GoonRock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoonRock "GoonRock")).[\[75\]](#cite_note-75) "Shape of You" fell by one position in the 2021 update of the chart.[\[76\]](#cite_note-76)

## Copyright trial

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Copyright trial")\]

In March 2022, Sheeran was taken to court by musicians Sami Chokri and Ross O'Donoghue who allege "Shape of You" infringes "particular lines and phrases" of their 2015 composition "Oh Why".[\[77\]](#cite_note-77) Sheeran and his co-writers, Steven McCutcheon and John McDaid, were suspended by music licensing body [PRS for Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRS_for_Music "PRS for Music") from collecting an estimated £20m in royalties from the performances or broadcasts of "Shape of You".[\[78\]](#cite_note-78)[\[79\]](#cite_note-79) Legal proceedings began in May 2018, with Sheeran and his co-writers asking the high court to declare they had not infringed Chokri and O'Donoghue's copyright. Two months later, Chokri and O'Donoghue issued their own claim for "copyright infringement, damages and an account of profits in relation to the alleged infringement".[\[80\]](#cite_note-80)

On 6 April 2022, the judge ruled that Sheeran had "neither deliberately nor subconsciously copied" Chokri's song. While there were "similarities between the one-bar phrase", the judge said that "differences between the relevant parts" of the songs were "compelling evidence that the 'Oh I' phrase" in Sheeran's song "originated from sources other than Oh Why".[\[81\]](#cite_note-81) After the win, Sheeran said: "I feel like claims like this are way too common now and have become a culture where a claim is made with the idea that a settlement will be cheaper than taking it to court, even if there's no basis for the claim. It's really damaging to the songwriting industry. There's only so many notes and very few chords used in pop music. Coincidence is bound to happen if 60,000 songs are being released every day on Spotify. That's 22 million songs a year, and there's only 12 notes that are available."[\[82\]](#cite_note-82)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Music video")\]

### Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Release")\]

On 30 January 2017, the official [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") of the song, paying homage to the [Rocky films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_\(franchise\) "Rocky (franchise)"), starring US dancer and model Jennie Pegouskie and retired professional [sumo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumo "Sumo") wrestler [Yamamotoyama Ryūta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamamotoyama_Ryūta "Yamamotoyama Ryūta") (credited as "Yama"), was released on Sheeran's channel.[\[85\]](#cite_note-85)[\[86\]](#cite_note-86) It was shot in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"), and was directed by Jason Koenig, who also directed Sheeran's fourth single "[Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_\(Ed_Sheeran_song\) "Perfect (Ed Sheeran song)")" from *[÷](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/÷_\(album\) "÷ (album)")*.[\[87\]](#cite_note-87)

### Synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Synopsis")\]

The music video opens with Sheeran, first seen sitting down in a lonely dark room save for the [sunlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunlight "Sunlight") that shines beside him, with footages featuring his love interest and fellow boxer (Jennie Pegouskie) and his upcoming match. As the song begins, we see Sheeran [shadowboxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadowboxing "Shadowboxing") while Pegouskie is already at the gym ready for the workout. She hangs herself at the punching bag doing sit-ups and stretches herself. A little while later, Pegouskie shadowboxes and punches a punching bag when Sheeran lately arrives at the training carrying a bag with him. After Sheeran places his bag at the closet, he proceeds to train himself for his upcoming match trained by a personal trainer along with Pegouskie who still warms herself up. Later, Sheeran and Pegouskie head out of the gym towards a restaurant while bonding each other. Upon arriving, the couple eat and share foods like canoodling over a fried chicken as they have an intimate conversation with each other, although their dialogue is entirely mute. Afterwards, Sheeran and his girlfriend ride a [taxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxi "Taxi") and [make out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Making_out "Making out") at the back seat while the taxi driver does not notice this as he is focusing on driving. Back at the gym, Sheeran and Pegouskie physically trained hard doing various training exercises. While training, the couple embraced each other and teach one other, eventually falling in love with each other in the process. Later, Pegouskie leaves a picture and a box to Sheeran in a closet and seemingly abandons him. The scene cuts back to Sheeran who discovers a picture and a black box both seen earlier with the latter containing a blue mouthguard featuring a **"÷"** symbol at the front. Realizing that his girlfriend had left him (unbeknownst to him, she already is on a ship), he starts to search for her to no avail. In response to her disappointing departure, Sheeran lets out his frustration and proceeds to an intense workout that includes tire-flipping, shadowboxing, sit-up, [running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running "Running") and [push-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push-up "Push-up"). Later, Sheeran participates a match he has anticipated throughout the clip but he unexpectedly encounters a [Rikishi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rikishi "Rikishi") or a [sumo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumo "Sumo") wrestler (Yamamotoyama Ryūta), much to his shock. During the match, Sheeran is seen almost always avoiding Yama who constantly chases him and the latter fails to defeat the Rikishi. Sheeran ends up getting defeated and is thrown at the edge of the [ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_ring "Boxing ring"), crying in agony with the crowd encouraging him to stand up. Towards the end of the video, Yama wins the match but Pegouskie emerges the scene among the crowd flying into the ring with a karate kick in the air aiming towards Yama as the scene cuts to black with the text that reads "DIRECTED BY: JASON KOENIG". Sheeran is last seen at the end of the music video struggling to get up while lying down on the floor, but he fails to do so.[\[88\]](#cite_note-88)[\[89\]](#cite_note-89)

### Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reception")\]

On 8 May 2017, 97 days after its release, it became one of the fastest music videos to reach 1 billion views on YouTube. As of February 2026, the music video has over 6\.6 billion views on YouTube, and is [the site's eighth most-watched video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos") as well as the third most-watched music video.[\[90\]](#cite_note-90)

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Sheeran performed "Shape of You" on *[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")* on 11 February 2017 and at the [59th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards") the following day.[\[91\]](#cite_note-91)[\[92\]](#cite_note-92) On 27 February, Sheeran performed the song on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")*, with [Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Fallon "Jimmy Fallon") and [The Roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Roots "The Roots"), who used classroom instruments.[\[93\]](#cite_note-93) On 6 July, Sheeran performed the track on US [breakfast television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakfast_television "Breakfast television") show *[Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_\(American_TV_program\) "Today (American TV program)")*.[\[94\]](#cite_note-94) On 27 August, Sheeran performed "Shape of You" at [2017 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2017 MTV Video Music Awards") in a [medley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medley_\(music\) "Medley (music)") with [Lil Uzi Vert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Uzi_Vert "Lil Uzi Vert") and his song "[XO Tour Llif3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XO_Tour_Llif3 "XO Tour Llif3")".[\[95\]](#cite_note-95) At the [NRJ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRJ_Music_Awards "NRJ Music Awards") 2017 on 4 November, he performed "Shape of You" in a [medley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medley_\(music\) "Medley (music)") with [Soprano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soprano_\(singer\) "Soprano (singer)") and his song "[Fresh Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresh_Prince_\(song\) "Fresh Prince (song)")".

## Remixes and covers

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Remixes and covers")\]

The official remix of "Shape of You" features newly additional verses and guest vocals by English [grime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grime_\(music_genre\) "Grime (music genre)") artist [Stormzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormzy "Stormzy"). The remix premiered during Sheeran and Stormzy's live collaboration at the [2017 Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Brit_Awards "2017 Brit Awards") at [The O2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_O2 "The O2") in London on 22 February 2017\.[\[96\]](#cite_note-96)

Sheeran announced on Twitter that the remix would be released officially on 24 February 2017\.[\[97\]](#cite_note-97) On the same date, various remixes of the song were released on [digital music services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_music "Digital music"). Sheeran teased the releases ahead of [2017 Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Brit_Awards "2017 Brit Awards") ceremony. "I've got two things dropping on Friday that are pretty interesting", he revealed in a BBC Radio 1 interview just hours before the big show. "One that gets debuted at the Brits, which I think people will go a bit nuts for." He added, "It's something that I think nobody is expecting. I think it'll be decent."[\[98\]](#cite_note-98)

In the United States, "Shape of You" has immediately become a favourite among DJs and remixers, prompting several of them to create their own versions. One DJ, [Joe "Maz" Masurka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Maz "Joe Maz"), told *Billboard* that after he did his own remix on the single that he received a lot of great feedback and response: "... the dance floor loves it."[\[99\]](#cite_note-99)

In April 2017, Aditya Rao, Vinod Krishnan and Mahesh Raghvan released a [carnatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnatic_music "Carnatic music") version of the song.[\[100\]](#cite_note-100) In September 2018, Ndlovu Youth Choir and Wouter Kellerman released "Shape of You" in Zulu version.[\[101\]](#cite_note-101)

## In other media

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: In other media")\]

In March 2017, a [Walsall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walsall "Walsall") woman Sonia Bryce was imprisoned for two months for [noise pollution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noise_pollution "Noise pollution") after repeatedly playing "Shape of You" at a high volume.[\[102\]](#cite_note-102)[\[103\]](#cite_note-103) English singer [Charli XCX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charli_XCX "Charli XCX") performed "Shape of You" in [drag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_\(clothing\) "Drag (clothing)") as Sheeran on the US television series *[Lip Sync Battle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lip_Sync_Battle "Lip Sync Battle")* in March 2018\.[\[104\]](#cite_note-104) The song is featured on the dance rhythm game, *[Just Dance 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_Dance_2018 "Just Dance 2018")*. It was featured and remixed in *[YouTube Rewind: The Shape of 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_Rewind#2017 "YouTube Rewind")*.[\[105\]](#cite_note-105) The song is also used in an episode in the French version of *[Skam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skam_\(TV_series\) "Skam (TV series)")*.[\[106\]](#cite_note-106) [Pentatonix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentatonix "Pentatonix") covered the song as a mash-up with "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")" for their 2018 album *[PTX Presents: Top Pop, Vol. I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PTX_Presents:_Top_Pop,_Vol._I "PTX Presents: Top Pop, Vol. I")*.[\[107\]](#cite_note-107)\[*[non-primary source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research#Primary,_secondary_and_tertiary_sources "Wikipedia:No original research")*\] Likewise, the song was covered by Hawaiian ukulele artist [Jake Shimabukuro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Shimabukuro "Jake Shimabukuro") for his 2018 album, *The Greatest Day*.[\[108\]](#cite_note-108) The song appears often in the Japanese drama [僕たちがやりました(We Did It/Fugitive Boys)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/僕たちがやりました#テレビドラマ "ja:僕たちがやりました").[\[109\]](#cite_note-109)\[*[non-primary source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research#Primary,_secondary_and_tertiary_sources "Wikipedia:No original research")*\][\[110\]](#cite_note-110)

The song also has been covered by [Postmodern Jukebox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmodern_Jukebox "Postmodern Jukebox"), done as a [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder")\-style 1970s number, guest starring [Stefano Langone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefano_Langone "Stefano Langone") on lead vocals. The video amassed three million views.[\[111\]](#cite_note-111) "Shape of You" has also been referenced in [Doja Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doja_Cat "Doja Cat")'s "[Get Into It (Yuh)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get_Into_It_\(Yuh\) "Get Into It (Yuh)")", from the album *[Planet Her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet_Her "Planet Her")* (2021). ["Weird Al" Yankovic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/"Weird_Al"_Yankovic "\"Weird Al\" Yankovic") covered the song for his 2024 polka medley "[Polkamania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_"Weird_Al"_Yankovic_polka_medleys#"Polkamania!" "List of \"Weird Al\" Yankovic polka medleys")!".

"**Shape of You**" is a song by English singer [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"). It was released on 6 January 2017 as one of the [double lead singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from his third studio album *[÷](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/÷_\(album\) "÷ (album)")* (2017), along with "[Castle on the Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_on_the_Hill "Castle on the Hill")". The [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall_pop "Dancehall pop") and [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues") infused song was written by Sheeran, [Steve Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Mac "Steve Mac") and [Johnny McDaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_McDaid "Johnny McDaid"). Due to its [interpolation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpolation_\(popular_music\) "Interpolation (popular music)") of "[No Scrubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Scrubs "No Scrubs")" by [TLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TLC_\(group\) "TLC (group)"), [Kandi Burruss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandi_Burruss "Kandi Burruss"), [Tameka "Tiny" Cottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tameka_Cottle "Tameka Cottle"), and [Kevin "She'kspere" Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_"She'kspere"_Briggs "Kevin \"She'kspere\" Briggs") are also credited as writers. The song was produced by Sheeran and Steve Mac.

Despite receiving mixed reviews from music critics, "Shape of You" peaked at number one on the singles charts of 34 countries, including the [US *Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100")—later becoming the [best performing song of 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2017 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2017")—as well as in the British, Australian, Canadian and Irish[\[2\]](#cite_note-IRE-2) singles charts. It stayed at number one for a record-tying 16 consecutive weeks on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), as well as 14 nonconsecutive weeks on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"), and 12 non-consecutive weeks on the Billboard Hot 100\. It was also highly successful elsewhere, reaching number one in many European charts and throughout [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America"),[\[3\]](#cite_note-ARG-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-COL-4) as well as in [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia") where it spent 12 non-consecutive weeks at the top.[\[5\]](#cite_note-MAL-5)

On 10 December 2018, the song became the first song to hit 2 billion streams on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"). On July 13, 2026, “Shape of You” became the second song to reach 5 billion streams on the platform and is currently the 2nd most streamed song overall, behind "[Blinding Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blinding_Lights "Blinding Lights")" by [The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd").[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) It was also the most-streamed song of the decade on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") with 2\.4 billion streams by December 2019, and the most streamed song on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") with 930 million streams, as of May 2023\. It was the best-selling song of 2017 and the decade in the UK. "Shape of You" was the best-selling song of 2017 and the second best-selling digital song worldwide, with combined sales and track-equivalent streams of 26\.6 million units according to [IFPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry").[\[7\]](#cite_note-ifpi_report-7)

In 2018, it sold an additional 14\.9 million copies, combining a total of 41\.5 million copies worldwide with the previous total sales figure, making it one of the [best selling digital singles of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_singles#Best-selling_digital_singles "List of best-selling singles"). Additionally, it made a second appearance in the *Billboard* year-end chart in 2018, at No. 71\.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) In 2019, it was named the number-one song on the *Billboard* [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") chart of the 2010s decade.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) "Shape of You" was nominated for [British Single of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Single "Brit Award for British Single") and [British Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_British_Video_of_the_Year "Brit Award for British Video of the Year") at the [2018 Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Brit_Awards "2018 Brit Awards").[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) The song won the [Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Pop_Solo_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Pop Solo Performance") at the [60th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/60th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "60th Annual Grammy Awards").[\[11\]](#cite_note-Grammys-11) In 2021, *Billboard* ranked "Shape of You" as the tenth most successful song of all time.[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

Written and recorded in 2016,[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) "Shape of You" was the final song added to Ed Sheeran's third album *[÷](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/÷_\(album\) "÷ (album)")*.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) As he had recently written all the songs he wanted for the album, the song was therefore not intended to be included in the album. It was first written for [Little Mix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Mix "Little Mix") and then it was conceived as a duet between [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") and [Rudimental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudimental "Rudimental"), but the head of the record label convinced him to keep the song for himself.[\[15\]](#cite_note-braca-15) He said:

> "\['Shape of You'\] is actually a really random one because I went in to write songs for other people with a guy called [Steve Mac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Mac "Steve Mac") and [Johnny McDaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_McDaid "Johnny McDaid"), and we were writing this song and I was like 'this would really work for Rihanna,'" he explained. "And then I started singing lyrics like 'putting [Van the Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Morrison "Van Morrison") on the jukebox' and I was like 'well she's not really going to sing that, is she?' And then we sort of decided halfway through that we were just going to make it for me."[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

According to Sheeran, Steve Mac started the songwriting session by playing the opening notes of the song on the keyboard. Sheeran then joined in, adding percussion by tapping on the guitar, layering it onto the track. On the writing of the song, he said that he tried to keep the music "more stripped" instead of something more elaborate: "I'm an [acoustic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_music "Acoustic music") artist, first and foremost. And when I play live, I can't replicate these things, I haven't got all the other musicians." Sheeran said he wanted an [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B") feel to the song, therefore he adjusted the original tune, adding an interpolation of "[No Scrubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Scrubs "No Scrubs")" onto part of the melody. He also revealed that the original lyrics did not end with the words "the shape of you" in the chorus, but during the writing of the song, McDaid thought that the lyrics "I'm in love with your body" sounded objectifying, and the lyrics was therefore adjusted.[\[17\]](#cite_note-nytimes-17)[\[15\]](#cite_note-braca-15) In a March 2023 interview with *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*, Sheeran revealed that he had attempted to get a [Jay-Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z") guest verse; Jay-Z declined, stating that he "doesn't think the song needs a [rap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapping "Rapping") verse".[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

## Release

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Release")\]

On 6 January 2017, when hosting *[The Radio 1 Breakfast Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Radio_1_Breakfast_Show "The Radio 1 Breakfast Show")*, Sheeran revealed that "Shape of You" was written with Rihanna in mind.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) On 4 January 2017, Sheeran uploaded a six-second teaser video of a blue background to social media, with lyrics "the club isn't the best place to find a lover", which is the first line of "Shape of You". To further tease the release, Sheeran and his label used a sponsored [Snapchat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapchat "Snapchat") lens filter with 30 seconds of the song to increase buzz among the general public.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Composition")\]

"Shape of You" has been characterised as [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"),[\[22\]](#cite_note-McIntyre-22) [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall"),[\[23\]](#cite_note-:0-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) and [tropical house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_house "Tropical house"),[\[25\]](#cite_note-Molanphy_2022-25) with "strummy acoustics".[\[26\]](#cite_note-auto-26) "Shape of You" is written in the key of [C-sharp minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-sharp_minor "C-sharp minor") with a tempo of 96 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute"). The song is composed in [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature") (**4**  
**4** time), and follows a basic [chord progression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chord_progression "Chord progression") of C♯m–F♯m–A–B (i–iv–VI–VII), and Sheeran's vocals span from G♯3 to G♯5.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) It has a [tresillo rhythm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tresillo_\(rhythm\) "Tresillo (rhythm)").[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)

In the song, Sheeran sings over a [marimba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marimba "Marimba")\-fueled percussive sway about a budding romance: "The club isn't the best place to find a lover, so the bar is where I go/ Me and my friends at the table doing shots drinking fast and then we talk slow", he sings. "Come over and start up a conversation with just me/ And trust me I'll give it a chance."[\[29\]](#cite_note-29)[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) According to *[NT News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NT_News "NT News")*, the song "tells the story of loved (or lusted) up Sheeran meeting a girl in a bar where he and his mates are doing shots."[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

The song's lyrical rhythm drew some comparisons to the 1999 [TLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TLC_\(group\) "TLC (group)") hit "[No Scrubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Scrubs "No Scrubs")", particularly in the pre-chorus line, "Boy, let's not talk too much/ Grab on my waist and put that body on me". Kandi Burruss had told Bravo's Andy Cohen that the negotiations had started before the song's release for its interpolation but weren't finalized until afterwards. As a result, the composers of "No Scrubs", [Kandi Burruss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandi_Burruss "Kandi Burruss"), [Tameka "Tiny" Cottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tameka_Cottle "Tameka Cottle"), and [Kevin "She'kspere" Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_"She'kspere"_Briggs "Kevin \"She'kspere\" Briggs"), received co-writing credits on "Shape of You".[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

The song received generally mixed reviews from music critics. [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") from *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* said, "'Shape of You' is trickier, a nimble and effective song that takes the aggressive thinning of '[Caribbean music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_music "Caribbean music")'."[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")*'s Taylor Weatherby wrote about the song saying, "'Shape of You' doesn't quite sound like your typical Sheeran tune. But that almost serves as an indication of what the '[Thinking Out Loud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thinking_Out_Loud "Thinking Out Loud")' singer has been up to during his hiatus: creating music that still feels like Sheeran, just with a new twist."[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) Jeremy Gordon of *[Spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_\(magazine\) "Spin (magazine)")* gave the song a positive review, stating that the song "is a plausible attempt at convincing us he has had sex ... a lot of it. It kind of slaps, though you can't really picture Sheeran ever saying 'put that body on me' to a real human woman."[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) *[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")* gave the song a B+ rating,[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) and *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* ranked the song at number 13 on its "50 best songs of 2017" list.[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) *[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")* ranked it at number 36 of 2017 singles.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)

*[Uproxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uproxx "Uproxx")* ranked the song at number 3 on its "The Worst Songs Of 2017" list: "The contrarian in me is always tempted to defend Ed Sheeran, because it's way too easy to take shots at this guy... Then I hear the part in 'Shape Of You' where he says, 'And last night you were in my room / And now my bedsheets smell like you.' And now I want to push him into a locker."[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) *Spin* and *[Esquire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esquire_\(magazine\) "Esquire (magazine)")* listed it as one of the worst songs of 2017\.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)[\[41\]](#cite_note-41)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"Shape of You" debuted at number one on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") on 13 January 2017, selling 227,000 combined units in its first week and becoming Sheeran's third UK number one. Sheeran also debuted at number two with the song "[Castle on the Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_on_the_Hill "Castle on the Hill")", making him the first artist in UK chart history to debut in the top two positions simultaneously.[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) It spent 13 consecutive weeks at number one,[\[43\]](#cite_note-weeks-43) and a further week at the top after a week's interruption by [Harry Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Styles "Harry Styles")' "[Sign of the Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sign_of_the_Times_\(Harry_Styles_song\) "Sign of the Times (Harry Styles song)")".[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) In July 2017, the song reached 184 million in streams, making it the most-streamed song in the UK of all time until November 2022, when it was overtaken by [Lewis Capaldi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Capaldi "Lewis Capaldi")'s "[Someone You Loved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Someone_You_Loved "Someone You Loved")".[\[45\]](#cite_note-45) It was the nation's highest selling and most streamed track of 2017 with 787,000 copies sold and 248 million streams throughout the year, to produce a combined sales of 3\.2 million.[\[46\]](#cite_note-Top40UK2017-46) In September 2020, the track was [certified eight-times platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_music_recording_certifications "List of music recording certifications") by the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI).[\[47\]](#cite_note-BPI-47) "Shape of You" is Sheeran's best-selling single in the UK with total sales of 5\.09 million units as of July 2021, according to the [Official Charts Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company").[\[48\]](#cite_note-OCC-48)

The song debuted at number one on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), selling 240,000 downloads and gaining 20 million streams in its debut week in the US, becoming Sheeran's first number one song in the country.[\[49\]](#cite_note-Billboard_record-49) Sheeran also became the first artist to debut two songs in the top 10 the same week in the history of the Hot 100, with "Castle on the Hill" also debuting at number six.[\[49\]](#cite_note-Billboard_record-49) "Shape of You" topped the Hot 100 for 12 non-consecutive weeks.[\[50\]](#cite_note-trust-50) In its fourth week at number one, the song also topped the [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40"), becoming Sheeran's second number-one single on the chart (after 2015's "Thinking Out Loud"). On 6 May 2017, it fell to number two on the Hot 100, being displaced by [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar")'s "[Humble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humble_\(song\) "Humble (song)")".[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) On the issue date, 2 September 2017, "Shape of You" spent its 32nd week in the top ten of Hot 100, tying the record for the most weeks on that chart with [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes")' "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")" and [the Chainsmokers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chainsmokers "The Chainsmokers")' "[Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer_\(The_Chainsmokers_song\) "Closer (The Chainsmokers song)")" featuring [Halsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halsey_\(singer\) "Halsey (singer)").[\[52\]](#cite_note-us_sales1-52) The following week, "Shape of You" spent its 33rd consecutive week in the top 10, breaking the 20-year-old record. This record would be tied twice and eventually broken in 2020 by [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone")'s "[Circles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circles_\(Post_Malone_song\) "Circles (Post Malone song)")."[\[53\]](#cite_note-53) On [*Billboard*'s Dance/Mix Show Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Mix_Show_Airplay "Dance/Mix Show Airplay") chart, "Shape of You" became Sheeran's first number one on a Dance/EDM chart (his third top ten and sixth overall at Dance/Mix Show Airplay) in the United States.[\[54\]](#cite_note-54) Afterwards, the song topped [Dance Club Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_Club_Songs "Dance Club Songs") in its 18 March 2017 issue, his first as a solo artist and his second entry on this chart, when he was a featured artist on Rudimental's "[Lay It All on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lay_It_All_on_Me_\(song\) "Lay It All on Me (song)")", which peaked at No. 38 in 2016\.[\[55\]](#cite_note-US_Dance_current_number_one-55)[\[56\]](#cite_note-56) By August 2017, "Shape of You" was the best selling song of 2017 in the US with 2\.3 million copies sold, the only one to sell over two million. It is also the most streamed song with 799\.7 million combined audio and video streams.[\[52\]](#cite_note-us_sales1-52) The song became the number one song of the year on *Billboard* Hot 100 in 2017,[\[57\]](#cite_note-57) and the second best-selling song in the US after "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")" with over 2\.5 million copies sold.[\[58\]](#cite_note-us_sales-58)

It debuted at number one in France,[\[59\]](#cite_note-France-59) and was later certified diamond there.[\[60\]](#cite_note-60) According to [Pure Charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pure_Charts "Pure Charts"), in the first half of the year 2017, the song reached 631,000 units (105,000 sales and 526,000 units from streams) and as of September 2017, it exceeds 812,109 units (707,109 from streams).[\[61\]](#cite_note-61) It was the best-selling song (including streaming) in France this year.[\[62\]](#cite_note-62) In [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts"), the song stayed at No. 1 for 15 weeks, breaking a record set 22 years ago by [Coolio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coolio "Coolio")'s "[Gangsta's Paradise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gangsta's_Paradise "Gangsta's Paradise")".[\[63\]](#cite_note-63) In doing this, it also broke ABBA's record of fourteen weeks at number one, which was set on the previous Australian charts before the ARIA charts became Australia's official charts.[\[64\]](#cite_note-64) "Shape of You" was also Australia's highest selling song of 2017 with 630,000 copies sold by the end of the year.[\[65\]](#cite_note-AustraliaEnd2017-65) The song is the first ever number one single of the now-defunct [Philippine Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Hot_100 "Philippine Hot 100") upon the chart's inception on 12 June 2017\.[\[66\]](#cite_note-66) It stayed at the peak position for 4 consecutive weeks before it was dethroned by "Despacito" by [Luis Fonsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Fonsi "Luis Fonsi") and [Daddy Yankee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daddy_Yankee "Daddy Yankee") featuring [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber").\[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*\]

Worldwide, the song reached one billion streams on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") in June 2017\.[\[67\]](#cite_note-67)[\[68\]](#cite_note-68) It became the most streamed song on Spotify in September 2017, reaching 1,318,420,396 streams overtaking [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)")'s "[One Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Dance "One Dance")".[\[69\]](#cite_note-spotify-69) It became the first song to reach [2 billions in streams on Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records "List of Spotify streaming records") in 2018,[\[70\]](#cite_note-forbes-70) and it was the most-streamed song of the decade on Spotify, with 2\.4 billion streams in the 2010s.[\[71\]](#cite_note-decade_stream-71) On 22 December 2021, "Shape of You" became Spotify's first song to hit 3 billion streams.[\[72\]](#cite_note-72) In May 2023, [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") announced that "Shape of You" was the most-streamed song on the platform, with over 930 million streams.[\[73\]](#cite_note-73)[\[74\]](#cite_note-74)

In August 2018, *Billboard* published a new edition of the "Greatest of All Time Hot 100 Singles" chart, its list of the 100 best-performing songs in the history of the Hot 100\. "Shape of You" was ranked at number nine, the third-highest position of any song released in the 2010s (behind only "[Uptown Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")" by [Mark Ronson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ronson "Mark Ronson") featuring [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars") and "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")" by [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO "LMFAO") featuring [Lauren Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauren_Bennett "Lauren Bennett") and [GoonRock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoonRock "GoonRock")).[\[75\]](#cite_note-75) "Shape of You" fell by one position in the 2021 update of the chart.[\[76\]](#cite_note-76)

## Copyright trial

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Copyright trial")\]

In March 2022, Sheeran was taken to court by musicians Sami Chokri and Ross O'Donoghue who allege "Shape of You" infringes "particular lines and phrases" of their 2015 composition "Oh Why".[\[77\]](#cite_note-77) Sheeran and his co-writers, Steven McCutcheon and John McDaid, were suspended by music licensing body [PRS for Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRS_for_Music "PRS for Music") from collecting an estimated £20m in royalties from the performances or broadcasts of "Shape of You".[\[78\]](#cite_note-78)[\[79\]](#cite_note-79) Legal proceedings began in May 2018, with Sheeran and his co-writers asking the high court to declare they had not infringed Chokri and O'Donoghue's copyright. Two months later, Chokri and O'Donoghue issued their own claim for "copyright infringement, damages and an account of profits in relation to the alleged infringement".[\[80\]](#cite_note-80)

On 6 April 2022, the judge ruled that Sheeran had "neither deliberately nor subconsciously copied" Chokri's song. While there were "similarities between the one-bar phrase", the judge said that "differences between the relevant parts" of the songs were "compelling evidence that the 'Oh I' phrase" in Sheeran's song "originated from sources other than Oh Why".[\[81\]](#cite_note-81) After the win, Sheeran said: "I feel like claims like this are way too common now and have become a culture where a claim is made with the idea that a settlement will be cheaper than taking it to court, even if there's no basis for the claim. It's really damaging to the songwriting industry. There's only so many notes and very few chords used in pop music. Coincidence is bound to happen if 60,000 songs are being released every day on Spotify. That's 22 million songs a year, and there's only 12 notes that are available."[\[82\]](#cite_note-82)

On 30 January 2017, the official [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") of the song, paying homage to the [Rocky films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_\(franchise\) "Rocky (franchise)"), starring US dancer and model Jennie Pegouskie and retired professional [sumo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumo "Sumo") wrestler [Yamamotoyama Ryūta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamamotoyama_Ryūta "Yamamotoyama Ryūta") (credited as "Yama"), was released on Sheeran's channel.[\[85\]](#cite_note-85)[\[86\]](#cite_note-86) It was shot in [Seattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"), and was directed by Jason Koenig, who also directed Sheeran's fourth single "[Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfect_\(Ed_Sheeran_song\) "Perfect (Ed Sheeran song)")" from *[÷](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/÷_\(album\) "÷ (album)")*.[\[87\]](#cite_note-87)

### Synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Synopsis")\]

The music video opens with Sheeran, first seen sitting down in a lonely dark room save for the [sunlight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunlight "Sunlight") that shines beside him, with footages featuring his love interest and fellow boxer (Jennie Pegouskie) and his upcoming match. As the song begins, we see Sheeran [shadowboxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shadowboxing "Shadowboxing") while Pegouskie is already at the gym ready for the workout. She hangs herself at the punching bag doing sit-ups and stretches herself. A little while later, Pegouskie shadowboxes and punches a punching bag when Sheeran lately arrives at the training carrying a bag with him. After Sheeran places his bag at the closet, he proceeds to train himself for his upcoming match trained by a personal trainer along with Pegouskie who still warms herself up. Later, Sheeran and Pegouskie head out of the gym towards a restaurant while bonding each other. Upon arriving, the couple eat and share foods like canoodling over a fried chicken as they have an intimate conversation with each other, although their dialogue is entirely mute. Afterwards, Sheeran and his girlfriend ride a [taxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxi "Taxi") and [make out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Making_out "Making out") at the back seat while the taxi driver does not notice this as he is focusing on driving. Back at the gym, Sheeran and Pegouskie physically trained hard doing various training exercises. While training, the couple embraced each other and teach one other, eventually falling in love with each other in the process. Later, Pegouskie leaves a picture and a box to Sheeran in a closet and seemingly abandons him. The scene cuts back to Sheeran who discovers a picture and a black box both seen earlier with the latter containing a blue mouthguard featuring a **"÷"** symbol at the front. Realizing that his girlfriend had left him (unbeknownst to him, she already is on a ship), he starts to search for her to no avail. In response to her disappointing departure, Sheeran lets out his frustration and proceeds to an intense workout that includes tire-flipping, shadowboxing, sit-up, [running](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running "Running") and [push-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Push-up "Push-up"). Later, Sheeran participates a match he has anticipated throughout the clip but he unexpectedly encounters a [Rikishi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rikishi "Rikishi") or a [sumo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumo "Sumo") wrestler (Yamamotoyama Ryūta), much to his shock. During the match, Sheeran is seen almost always avoiding Yama who constantly chases him and the latter fails to defeat the Rikishi. Sheeran ends up getting defeated and is thrown at the edge of the [ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_ring "Boxing ring"), crying in agony with the crowd encouraging him to stand up. Towards the end of the video, Yama wins the match but Pegouskie emerges the scene among the crowd flying into the ring with a karate kick in the air aiming towards Yama as the scene cuts to black with the text that reads "DIRECTED BY: JASON KOENIG". Sheeran is last seen at the end of the music video struggling to get up while lying down on the floor, but he fails to do so.[\[88\]](#cite_note-88)[\[89\]](#cite_note-89)

### Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reception")\]

On 8 May 2017, 97 days after its release, it became one of the fastest music videos to reach 1 billion views on YouTube. As of February 2026, the music video has over 6\.6 billion views on YouTube, and is [the site's eighth most-watched video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos") as well as the third most-watched music video.[\[90\]](#cite_note-90)

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Sheeran performed "Shape of You" on *[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")* on 11 February 2017 and at the [59th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "59th Annual Grammy Awards") the following day.[\[91\]](#cite_note-91)[\[92\]](#cite_note-92) On 27 February, Sheeran performed the song on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")*, with [Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Fallon "Jimmy Fallon") and [The Roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Roots "The Roots"), who used classroom instruments.[\[93\]](#cite_note-93) On 6 July, Sheeran performed the track on US [breakfast television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakfast_television "Breakfast television") show *[Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_\(American_TV_program\) "Today (American TV program)")*.[\[94\]](#cite_note-94) On 27 August, Sheeran performed "Shape of You" at [2017 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2017 MTV Video Music Awards") in a [medley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medley_\(music\) "Medley (music)") with [Lil Uzi Vert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Uzi_Vert "Lil Uzi Vert") and his song "[XO Tour Llif3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XO_Tour_Llif3 "XO Tour Llif3")".[\[95\]](#cite_note-95) At the [NRJ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NRJ_Music_Awards "NRJ Music Awards") 2017 on 4 November, he performed "Shape of You" in a [medley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medley_\(music\) "Medley (music)") with [Soprano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soprano_\(singer\) "Soprano (singer)") and his song "[Fresh Prince](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresh_Prince_\(song\) "Fresh Prince (song)")".

## Remixes and covers

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Remixes and covers")\]

The official remix of "Shape of You" features newly additional verses and guest vocals by English [grime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grime_\(music_genre\) "Grime (music genre)") artist [Stormzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stormzy "Stormzy"). The remix premiered during Sheeran and Stormzy's live collaboration at the [2017 Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Brit_Awards "2017 Brit Awards") at [The O2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_O2 "The O2") in London on 22 February 2017\.[\[96\]](#cite_note-96)

Sheeran announced on Twitter that the remix would be released officially on 24 February 2017\.[\[97\]](#cite_note-97) On the same date, various remixes of the song were released on [digital music services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_music "Digital music"). Sheeran teased the releases ahead of [2017 Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Brit_Awards "2017 Brit Awards") ceremony. "I've got two things dropping on Friday that are pretty interesting", he revealed in a BBC Radio 1 interview just hours before the big show. "One that gets debuted at the Brits, which I think people will go a bit nuts for." He added, "It's something that I think nobody is expecting. I think it'll be decent."[\[98\]](#cite_note-98)

In the United States, "Shape of You" has immediately become a favourite among DJs and remixers, prompting several of them to create their own versions. One DJ, [Joe "Maz" Masurka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Maz "Joe Maz"), told *Billboard* that after he did his own remix on the single that he received a lot of great feedback and response: "... the dance floor loves it."[\[99\]](#cite_note-99)

In April 2017, Aditya Rao, Vinod Krishnan and Mahesh Raghvan released a [carnatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnatic_music "Carnatic music") version of the song.[\[100\]](#cite_note-100) In September 2018, Ndlovu Youth Choir and Wouter Kellerman released "Shape of You" in Zulu version.[\[101\]](#cite_note-101)

## In other media

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Shape_of_You&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: In other media")\]

In March 2017, a [Walsall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walsall "Walsall") woman Sonia Bryce was imprisoned for two months for [noise pollution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noise_pollution "Noise pollution") after repeatedly playing "Shape of You" at a high volume.[\[102\]](#cite_note-102)[\[103\]](#cite_note-103) English singer [Charli XCX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charli_XCX "Charli XCX") performed "Shape of You" in [drag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_\(clothing\) "Drag (clothing)") as Sheeran on the US television series *[Lip Sync Battle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lip_Sync_Battle "Lip Sync Battle")* in March 2018\.[\[104\]](#cite_note-104) The song is featured on the dance rhythm game, *[Just Dance 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_Dance_2018 "Just Dance 2018")*. It was featured and remixed in *[YouTube Rewind: The Shape of 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_Rewind#2017 "YouTube Rewind")*.[\[105\]](#cite_note-105) The song is also used in an episode in the French version of *[Skam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skam_\(TV_series\) "Skam (TV series)")*.[\[106\]](#cite_note-106) [Pentatonix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentatonix "Pentatonix") covered the song as a mash-up with "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")" for their 2018 album *[PTX Presents: Top Pop, Vol. I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PTX_Presents:_Top_Pop,_Vol._I "PTX Presents: Top Pop, Vol. I")*.[\[107\]](#cite_note-107)\[*[non-primary source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research#Primary,_secondary_and_tertiary_sources "Wikipedia:No original research")*\] Likewise, the song was covered by Hawaiian ukulele artist [Jake Shimabukuro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Shimabukuro "Jake Shimabukuro") for his 2018 album, *The Greatest Day*.[\[108\]](#cite_note-108) The song appears often in the Japanese drama [僕たちがやりました(We Did It/Fugitive Boys)](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/僕たちがやりました#テレビドラマ "ja:僕たちがやりました").[\[109\]](#cite_note-109)\[*[non-primary source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research#Primary,_secondary_and_tertiary_sources "Wikipedia:No original research")*\][\[110\]](#cite_note-110)

The song also has been covered by [Postmodern Jukebox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmodern_Jukebox "Postmodern Jukebox"), done as a [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder")\-style 1970s number, guest starring [Stefano Langone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefano_Langone "Stefano Langone") on lead vocals. The video amassed three million views.[\[111\]](#cite_note-111) "Shape of You" has also been referenced in [Doja Cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doja_Cat "Doja Cat")'s "[Get Into It (Yuh)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get_Into_It_\(Yuh\) "Get Into It (Yuh)")", from the album *[Planet Her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet_Her "Planet Her")* (2021). ["Weird Al" Yankovic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/"Weird_Al"_Yankovic "\"Weird Al\" Yankovic") covered the song for his 2024 polka medley "[Polkamania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_"Weird_Al"_Yankovic_polka_medleys#"Polkamania!" "List of \"Weird Al\" Yankovic polka medleys")!".
